headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from Rasa-to-Taipy handoff; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can ingest external chat content via Messenger/Slack/Telegram/Twilio, and Taipy has no documented input-provenance controls or shared-channel protections. If Rasa outputs are forwarded into Taipy workflows, attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are copied or forwarded into Taipy inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF Taipy treats imported text as instructions or workflow parameters, attacker content can steer execution.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and schema around all Rasa-to-Taipy text.
Require manual approval before Taipy consumes any Rasa-generated content.
Strip markdown, code fences, and imperative phrases from inbound text.
Log provenance for each transferred message.
requires-engineering: implement content-signing or provenance tags across the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and can egress to allowlisted endpoints, but Taipy is documented with no network egress and no data classes touched. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage between them is not established. The main risk is limited to unusual operator wiring.
conditions: IF both agents are placed on the same shared filesystem, copied artifacts could leak.
IF Rasa is configured to send transcripts containing sensitive text to allowlisted third parties, that data may leave the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable transcript export unless needed.
Review allowlisted egress destinations in Rasa.
Use redacted sample data for Taipy inputs.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls between the two runtimes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not runnable and supports no multiple instances; Taipy has no documented write or network capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface, direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not expose a common writable target.
conditions: IF an operator mounts the same writable directory into both runtimes, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF Taipy is extended with write access to shared state, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Run each agent under a separate OS user.
Serialize any handoff through a single queue.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared database or filesystem.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa is a conversational agent that can generate user-facing text, and Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that may consume upstream outputs. If Taipy treats Rasa output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream workflows. The interaction is inferred from documented roles rather than directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes the rating upward.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests Rasa output without validation, incorrect text can propagate into workflows.
IF Taipy triggers automation from Rasa-generated content, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Taipy consumes Rasa output.
Require human review for any action-triggering message.
Limit Taipy to read-only reporting on Rasa outputs.
Add unit tests for representative Rasa responses.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and rejection paths.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Rasa touches text and voice, while Taipy lists no data classes touched, so a compliance breach is not evidenced. Because no specific regulated-data pathway is documented, only a low residual risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Rasa into a non-compliant deployment, compliance obligations may apply.
IF Taipy is configured to retain imported records longer than policy allows, retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Confirm retention settings before deployment.
Keep deployment region and storage policy documented.
Use synthetic data for testing.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
